newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-MARSEILLE DRAW FIRST BLOOD IN FEUD OVER CUP TIE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MARSEILLE DRAW FIRST BLOOD IN FEUD OVER CUP TIE.

text.p: Marseille drew first blood in their French Cup first round battle against Lille on Saturday without kicking a ball.

The former European champions, no strangers to controversy in the 1990s, failed to turn up for the match at Lille's home ground in northern France in the latest chapter in a tug-of-war over where it should be played.

Less than an hour later, the French Football Federation (FFF), which on Friday ordered the match be played in Lille, bowed to a civil court decision which favoured Marseille by effectively drawing out the dispute.

Former French international Dominique Bathenay, head of the FFF's French Cup commission, said: "It will be replayed (eds: correct) before the draw for the next round which takes place on January 23 and probably on a neutral ground."
"Olympique Marseille are habitues of the courts. If we are no longer masters of our competition, we can perhaps look ahead to less sad days," he added sarcastically.
Marseille have refused all along to travel to Lille for the match, which, when the first round draw was made on January 3, was due to be played in Marseille.
Unable to hold the match at home because of 1998 World Cup alterations being carried out at the Velodrome, Marseille wanted to exercise their right to stage it at a nearby neutral ground.
But they failed to advise the FFF within a two-day period and forfeited that right, handing the venue to their opponents in accordance with FFF regulations.
Marseille tabled an appeal, but the FFF refused it on Friday and ordered them to play at Lille.
So Marseille, who were relegated from the first division after being embroiled in a huge match-rigging scandal in 1991, went to the civil courts.
"We don't at all want to go to Lille, to be taken for the fools in this farce," Marseille chief executive Jean-Michel Roussier said.
When the civil court decided to postpone for a month a decision on the FFF ruling, Marseille opted not to travel to Lille on Saturday.
The second round is in three week's time and a month's wait for a court decision would cause serious disruption to the competition.
